title: Walter Shewhart and the Invention of the Control Chart (1924)
explainer: In a one-page internal memo at Bell Labs in May 1924, physicist and statistician Walter Shewhart introduced the control chart: a simple way to tell whether variation in a process is normal ('common cause') or a sign that something has actually changed ('special cause'). The same logic underlies model-monitoring dashboards in lightweight MLOps: tracking a metric over time and flagging departures from its normal range is a direct descendant of Shewhart's century-old method for catching drift in a process before it causes real defects.

title: DevOpsDays and the Founding of the DevOps Movement (2009)
explainer: The DevOps movement traces to a specific event: the first DevOpsDays conference, organized by Belgian IT consultant Patrick Debois in Ghent in 2009, which brought together people frustrated by the wall between writing software and running it in production. Lightweight MLOps is, in large part, that same argument applied to machine learning: breaking down the separation between training a model and being responsible for how it behaves once deployed, which is why 'MLOps' is less a brand-new discipline than DevOps's lesson re-learned for models.
